newsitem.title: UK: Willis-no comment on German link-up talk.
newsitem.headline: Willis-no comment on German link-up talk.

text.p: British insurance broker Willis Corroon declined to comment on Thursday on reports it was in talks over global co-operation with Germany's largest insurance broker Jauch & Huebener.
German industry sources said Jauch & Huebener was in discussions with Willis, J & H Marsh & McLennan of the U.S and British-based Sedgwick Group.
No-one at Sedgwick was available to comment.

Sedgwick, which has missed out on the hectic consolidation in the industry but has never ruled out the possibility of a merger, was again at the centre of takeover talk with U.S. giant Aon Corp ready to pounce according to U.S. industry sources.
After results in February, Sedgwick chairman Sax Riley predicted a second round of consolidation was about to begin in the industry.
Sedgwick shares closed the day 3-1/2 pence higher at 128-1/2 pence.

The report of talks with Jauch & Huebener follows the recent merger of Marsh McLennan with Johnson & Higgins, until now the German company's partner in UNISON, an international network of independent insurance brokers.

A spokesman for Jauch & Huebener refused to comment on the names of possible future partners, but said that "talks are being held with a number of international broking firms over possible co-operation".
He added that this could involve a foreign partner taking a minority stake in Jauch & Huebener.
